The current implementation forces `TypeNameHandling.All` (as it is the only way to encode the root type) which was quite a surprise - the primary reason we chose JSON as the serialization format for our grain states was to allow some backwards/forwards compatibility when changing grain state structure, but we can't change type names at the moment (even if the data structure remains identical).

issue_context.title: InvalidCastException when deserializing json state when custom JsonProperty is used with TypeNameHandling.None
issue_context.body:
`InvalidCastException` is thrown when deserializing json state using the Azure Table Storage provider if the state was serialized with properties having the `JsonProperty` attribute with a redefining property name. The exception is thrown if the state is stored with `TypeNameHandling.None`.

A PR is coming...

review_comments: My only question about this PR is whether or not there might be backwards compatibility concerns. What do you think, @rmja?

@ReubenBond I am pretty sure that it is safe. Note that it is the same approach as in the [Redis provider](https://github.com/OrleansContrib/Orleans.StorageProvider.Redis/blob/master/RedisStorage/RedisStorage.cs#L117).
Thanks, I think you're correct. It might be worth adding a test, though, since an issue here may leave users stranded.
